extracted.intended_audience: investigators, departmental administrators, and sponsored programs staff preparing NIH research grant budgets (SF424 (R&R) and PHS398 applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and justifying budgets for NIH research grant applications, including distinctions between modular and detailed budgets, allowable costs, F&A (indirect) cost treatment, consortium/subaward rules, and narrative justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost allowability and tests for costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs charged to awards must be allowable, allocable, reasonable, necessary, and consistently applied. NIH may disallow costs that do not meet these tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant's budget request is reviewed for compliance with governing cost principles and policies applicable to the recipient and award type. See NIH Grants Policy Statement Section 7.2 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the funding opportunity for limits and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read the funding opportunity for budget criteria, including limits on expense types, caps on certain expenses, and overall funding limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant funding opportunity sections include II.1 (Mechanism of Support), II.2 (Funds Available), III.2 (Cost Sharing or Matching), and IV.5 (Funding Restrictions). Examples: no construction allowed; travel limited to a specified dollar amount; total costs cannot exceed a yearly cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request only necessary and reasonable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify all the costs that are necessary and reasonable to complete the work described in the proposal and request a reasonable amount of money — not more and not less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers judge whether costs are justified by aims and methods and will look at person months to see if effort aligns with expectations. Significant over- or under-estimating suggests poor understanding of scope. Cost-sharing normally does not affect evaluation except for select programs requiring it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency and rounding requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Round to whole dollars and use only U.S. dollars throughout the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these conventions when preparing budget line items and totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct costs versus F&A (indirect) costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct costs can be identified specifically with a particular sponsored project; F&A costs are necessary costs benefiting more than one cost objective and not readily assignable to a specific project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total requested costs include allowable direct costs plus allowable F&A. F&A are determined by applying your organization's negotiated F&A rate to your direct cost base. General purpose equipment and routine administrative costs are normally treated as F&A.

rubrics_metrics.name: F&A rate determination and negotiation
rubrics_metrics.description: F&A costs are determined by the recipient's negotiated F&A rate with a cognizant federal agency; for-profit organizations negotiate with Division of Cost Allocation (DFAS/DCA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most non-profits, educational and hospital institutions have negotiated rates with HHS or other agencies. Check with your sponsored programs office for your negotiated rate and direct cost base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct cost base and MTDC exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The negotiated F&A rate will often use a modified total direct cost (MTDC) base, which excludes certain items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common exclusions include equipment, student tuition, research patient care costs, rent, and sub-recipient charges after the first $25,000. Check institution-specific agreements to confirm the MTDC base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular versus detailed budget format
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses two budget formats: R&R Budget Form (detailed) and PHS398 Modular Budget (modular). The chosen format depends on total direct costs requested and activity code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modular format is used to request up to $250,000 direct costs per year (in $25,000 modules) for some applications. An application will include either the R&R Budget Form or the PHS398 Modular Budget Form, not both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular budget exclusions and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The modular budget format is NOT accepted for SBIR/STTR grant applications or applications from foreign (non-U.S.) institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If modular is not allowed for your application type, use the detailed budget even if your direct costs would otherwise qualify for modular.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to create a modular budget and determine modules
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the PHS398 Modular Budget form and follow electronic application user's guide instructions; do not submit SF424 (R&R) Budget form when using PHS398.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine number of modules, subtract any consortium F&A from total direct costs and round to the nearest $25,000 increment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular budget justification components — Personnel Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel Justification should include the name, role, and number of person-months devoted to the project for every person on the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include salary and fringe benefit rates in the modular personnel justification, but consider the legislatively mandated salary cap when determining modules. Use current cap when preparing modular budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular budget justification components — Consortium Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a consortium/subcontract, include total costs (direct + F&A) rounded to the nearest $1,000 for each consortium/subcontract and list personnel roles and person-months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate if the consortium is foreign. Personnel who are not employed by applicant organization should be listed on consortium pages as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular budget justification components — Additional Narrative Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Include explanations for variations in modules across years, describe any direct costs excluded from total direct costs (e.g., equipment, tuition remission), and describe any off-site work or foreign study sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These narratives help reviewers understand year-to-year changes and excluded costs; also aid auditors and institutional budgeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed budget — list all applicant organization personnel with base salary and effort
rubrics_metrics.description: All personnel from the applicant organization dedicating effort should be listed on the personnel budget with their base salary and effort, even if salary support is not requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives NIH staff current information to apply salary caps and to understand actual institutional investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort reporting in person months
rubrics_metrics.description: Report effort as person months rather than percent effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIH Usage of Person Months FAQs for help converting percent effort to person months; reviewers compare person months to proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary cap policy and how to budget salaries
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will not pay requested salary above the annual salary cap; if salary requested exceeds the cap NIH will reduce that line item at award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For detailed budgets, base requests on actual institutional base salaries (not the cap) so NIH can apply the appropriate salary cap at award. If caps increase in future years, recipients may rebudget up to new caps but NIH will not increase total award amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits rate guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe benefits rates are based on institutional policy; NIH does not set a pre-set fringe benefit limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult your sponsored programs office for which items to include and what rate to use. More on fringe benefits in the Grants Policy Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Personnel inclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Include senior/key personnel from the applicant organization who are dedicating effort; exclude 'Other Significant Contributors' who dedicate negligible effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultants or collaborators not employed by the applicant organization should not be included in section A but in section F.3 (consultants) or in the consortium/subaward budget (collaborators). Examples of other significant contributors: CEOs providing leadership but no direct contribution; mentors for K awardees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral associate listing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdocs can be listed in section A or B depending on involvement in project design and execution; if listed in section B include individuals' names and level of effort in the budget justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place postdocs where their role (design/execution vs training) is most appropriate and justify effort in the narrative when listed in section B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate student listing and tuition remission
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate students can be listed in section A or B; tuition remission is entered in section F.8 and is subject to graduate student compensation limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include students' names and level of effort in the budget justification if placed in section B. Check NIH Fiscal Policies/NRSA stipend levels for current guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other personnel and clerical/secretarial costs
rubrics_metrics.description: List other personnel by project role; if multiple people share a role indicate the number and combine person months and salaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretarial/clerical staff salaries are normally treated as F&A; direct charging may be appropriate if administrative or clerical services can be specifically identified to the project and are a major project cost. Be specific in justifications for other personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment definition and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment is defined as property with an acquisition cost of $5,000 or more (unless institution sets lower) and expected service life > 1 year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equipment is generally excluded from the F&A base. If requesting equipment already available, justify why current equipment is insufficient and how new equipment will be allocated to the project. General purpose equipment (desktops, laptops) should not be direct costs unless primarily used for the proposed research. Including price quotes can aid evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel justification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the budget justification include destination, number of people traveling, and dates or duration for anticipated travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state how travel is directly related to proposed research (e.g., presenting research at a conference vs. 'staying current'). Follow institutional travel policy or U.S. federal travel regulation if no institutional policy exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee costs entry guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave trainee costs section blank unless otherwise stated in the funding opportunity; graduate student tuition remission goes in section F.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specific funding opportunity instructions regarding trainee support; do not include unless allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and supplies itemization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate general categories (e.g., glassware, chemicals, animal costs) and an amount for each category in the budget justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories with costs less than $1,000 do not need to be itemized. Be clear about how estimates were developed for large or unusual items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal costs justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details on animal costs including number of animals, purchase price, and facility per diem care rate when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include more specific details about how you developed the estimate, especially if animal care costs are unusually large or small, to avoid reviewer confusion and recommended cuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and dissemination costs
rubrics_metrics.description: You may include costs associated with disseminating research findings; for new applications consider delaying publication costs until later budget periods once data are obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget publication costs prudently and justify timing within the project lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultant services versus consortiums
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants provide advice and should not be making research direction decisions; consultants typically charge a fixed rate that may include direct and F&A costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how much of consultant costs will be spent on travel. Consultants are not subject to the salary cap but should meet institutional definitions of reasonableness. Collaborators or subawardees making research decisions are treated as consortium/subaward entities, not consultants.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADP/computer services allowable charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Include research-specific computer services (e.g., supercomputer time, specialized software) in ADP/computer services; do not include standard desktop/laptop costs or routine tech support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard office computing costs are normally F&A; include only research-specific computing charges as direct costs when justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alterations and renovations (A&R) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A&R does not include general maintenance or projects exceeding $500,000 (construction); A&R can be used for projects like altering a room for new grant equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify basis for costs, itemize by category, enter total funds requested and where applicable provide square footage and costs. If A&R costs exceed $300,000, further limitations and additional documentation apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research patient care costs guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting inpatient/outpatient patient care costs, provide names of hospitals/clinics and amounts requested, separate inpatient and outpatient details, cost breakdowns, number of days and patients, and justify standard vs research care costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These costs are rare; justify thoroughly. If associated with patient accrual, restrictions may be justified in the Notice of Award. See NIH Grants Policy Statement for detailed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition budgeting guidance for graduate students
rubrics_metrics.description: In the budget justification include your school's tuition rates (in-state and out-of-state if applicable); you may need to budget less than full tuition to meet graduate student compensation limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to graduate student compensation limit and NRSA stipend levels; include tuition costs in section F.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid requesting clearly unallowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Some types of costs (e.g., entertainment costs) are not allowed under federal grants; requesting unallowable costs may result in NIH discounting them from the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure whether a cost is allowable, contact your sponsored programs office or the grants management specialist listed on the funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium/subaward budget and F&A rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For detailed budgets, each consortium must have an independent budget form. Consortium costs are subject to their respective cost principles and specific F&A rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-tier subawards' total cost is part of the primary applicant's direct costs for MTDC calculation. Consortium F&A costs are NOT included as part of the direct cost base when determining modular eligibility. The first $25,000 of each consortium's costs may be included in MTDC for F&A calculation if institutional agreement permits. If consortium is foreign, F&A for the consortium is limited to 8%. For-profit consortium partners must have a negotiated F&A rate to charge F&A; the default 40% small business rate applies only to SBIR/STTR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium justification separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each consortium should provide a separate budget justification addressing only items that pertain to the consortium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep consortium justifications distinct from the primary recipient's justification to clarify roles, costs, and allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgeting for out years and year-to-year variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide reasonable approximations for out-year budgets and be thorough enough to convince reviewers you understand overall costs; describe large year-to-year variations in the justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH does not have a standard policy on salary escalation in applications; request actual costs needed for each budget period and request escalations only if consistent with institutional policy. Explain any large variations (e.g., consultants only in final year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award rebudgeting and prior approval needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have latitude to rebudget within and between categories to meet unanticipated needs, but some changes require NIH prior written approval, particularly those involving change in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult NIH Grants Policy Statement - Changes in Project and Budget for specifics on what changes need prior approval versus those that can be done at recipient discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application budget reviewed for compliance and award consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant's budget request will be reviewed for compliance with cost principles and other requirements; any resulting award will include a budget consistent with these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare your budget so it aligns with federal cost principles and institutional policies to avoid adjustments or disallowances at award or audit.
